interest: Shows how Japan's 'population problem' fueled imperial expansion, with census data, Tokyo's growth, Brazil emigration, and U.S. military demographic assessments.
overview: This file (State Department decimal file 894.5011, File 959) covers economic and demographic intelligence on Japan from April 1930 to May 1938, focusing primarily on national census returns, demographic pressures, urbanization, and overseas migration. Comprising diplomatic despatches, consular reports, cross-reference sheets with attached periodic report extracts, commercial inquiries, and a War Department G-2 intelligence report, the collection documents the execution and results of the second (1930) and fourth (1935) decennial national censuses, annual natural population increases, and local registration data. Major themes include governmental responses to Japan's perceived 'over-population' crisis—such as the draft recommendations of the Food and Population Commission and state-assisted emigration to Brazil—as well as the rapid expansion of industrial metropolises like Tokyo, Osaka, and Nagoya, demographic developments across colonial territories (Chosen, Taiwan, Karafuto, Kwantung Leased Territory, and the South Seas Mandate), and military assessments of Japanese imperial manpower.

people.name: William C. Crane

subfiles.about: Recommendations approved by the population section of the Food and Population Commission toward solving Japan's population problem.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference sheet with a 1930 Tokyo report extract on Japan's Food and Population Commission recommendations: a new Social Department, a standing inquiry body, and distribution and consumption measures.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference Sheet with Attached Extract on Recommendations of the Food and Population Commission

subfiles.about: Preparations and anticipated unemployment data for the second regular decennial census of October 1, 1930.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference sheet with a 1930 Tokyo report extract noting preparations for Japan's second decennial census: 250,000 enumerators, 4,000,000 yen cost, expected to reveal previously underestimated unemployment.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference Sheet with Attached Extract on Preparations for the 1930 Decennial Census

subfiles.about: Initial returns and regional population growth from the concluding of Japan's second decennial census.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference sheet with a November 1930 Tokyo report extract on initial second census results, with growth figures for Hokkaido, Karafuto, and Chosen, and Nagoya's premature celebration of reaching one million residents.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference Sheet with Attached Extract on Initial Results of the Second Decennial Census

subfiles.about: Inquiry from the editor of Compton's Pictured Encyclopedia requesting recent population figures for Japan and its major cities.
subfiles.summary: Compton's Pictured Encyclopedia editor Athol E. Rollins asks the State Department for current population figures for Japan and its major cities before the encyclopedia goes to press.
subfiles.title: Letter from Compton & Company Requesting Japanese Census Statistics

subfiles.about: Transmittal of Compton's Encyclopedia's population inquiry to the Bureau of Foreign and Domestic Commerce for direct response.
keywords: Bureau of Foreign and Domestic Commerce
subfiles.summary: Memo refers Rollins's census inquiry to the Bureau of Foreign and Domestic Commerce for direct reply.
subfiles.title: Department of State Memorandum Referring Compton Inquiry to Bureau of Foreign and Domestic Commerce
subfiles.to: Bureau of Foreign and Domestic Commerce

subfiles.about: State Department letter notifying Compton's Encyclopedia that its inquiry was referred to the Bureau of Foreign and Domestic Commerce.
keywords: Bureau of Foreign and Domestic Commerce
subfiles.summary: State Department tells Rollins that consular economic reports go to the Commerce Department's Bureau of Foreign and Domestic Commerce, which handles public dissemination, and that his letter was forwarded there.
subfiles.title: Department of State Letter to Athol E. Rollins Regarding Census Inquiry

subfiles.about: Consular report analyzing Japanese Foreign Office statistics on Japanese subjects resident abroad and state-assisted emigration to Brazil.
subfiles.summary: This sub-file includes a cross-reference sheet (894.5011/26) and a detailed four-page report prepared by Consul General Arthur Garrels in Tokyo on December 4, 1930. Sourced from the Japanese Foreign Office, it analyzes emigration trends from 1920 to 1929, recording 759,435 Japanese subjects living abroad as of October 1, 1929. The report focuses on government-assisted emigration to Brazil following exclusion in the United States and Australia, providing tables of annual assisted emigrants and a worldwide geographical distribution of Japanese residents by country.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference Sheet and Report by Garrels on Japanese Subjects Resident Abroad

subfiles.about: Diplomatic despatch transmitting official 1930 decennial census returns for the Japanese Empire and principal cities.
subfiles.summary: Despatch No. 84: Forbes reports the October 1930 census found the Japanese Empire's population at 90,395,041 (up 7.9% since 1925), with Japan proper at 64,447,724, city tabulations, and plans to annex Tokyo's suburbs into a nearly five-million metropolis.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 84 from Forbes Reporting Results of the 1930 Decennial Census

subfiles.about: Consular report summarizing preliminary returns and international comparisons for the third Japanese national census of 1930.
subfiles.summary: Report No. 70: Garrels gives preliminary 1930 census figures, comparing Japan's population density to Belgium, Holland, and England, with sex ratios, urban concentration, growth rates since 1920, and counts for the seven largest cities.
subfiles.title: Report No. 70 by Garrels on Preliminary Figures for the Third National Census

subfiles.about: Transmittal of a corrected page for an earlier consular report on Japanese population growth and over-population.
subfiles.summary: Despatch No. 346: Garrels transmits a corrected page for Sturgeon's report on Japanese over-population, revising Japanese residing abroad to 800,000 and the annual population increase to 900,000.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 346 from Garrels Transmitting Corrected Page for Report on Over-Population

subfiles.about: Consular report analyzing preliminary results of the fourth national census of Japan taken on October 1, 1935.
subfiles.summary: Consul J. Holbrook Chapman reviews preliminary returns of the fourth national census of October 1, 1935, announced by the Cabinet's Bureau of General Statistics. The population of the Japanese Empire reached 97,694,628 (and 99,453,629 including leased and mandated zones), an 8.1 percent increase over 1930. The report highlights accelerating urbanization, sex ratios, demographic data for Chosen, Taiwan, Karafuto, Kwantung Leased Territory, and the South Manchuria Railway Zone, and explains how Tokyo's dramatic rise to 5,875,388 resulted from prefectural municipal amalgamations.
subfiles.title: Report No. 166 by Chapman on Preliminary Announced Results of the Fourth National Census

subfiles.about: Reporting of Cabinet statistics showing the natural population increase in Japan for the first half of 1935.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference sheet with a 1936 extract reporting a 565,915 natural population increase in Japan for the first half of 1935, up 103,935 over the same period in 1934.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference Sheet with Attached Extract on Natural Increase in Population for Early 1935

subfiles.about: Reporting of press data showing that Japan's population increase in 1935 was the greatest annual gain since 1898.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference sheet with a 1936 extract reporting Japan's 1935 population increase of 1,028,623, the largest annual gain since official statistics began in 1898.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference Sheet with Attached Extract on Record Population Increase for 1935

subfiles.about: Notice of a voluntary report from Yokohama on the problem of Japanese surplus population.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference sheet to a 1937 report by Consul Boyce from Yokohama on 'The Problem of the Japanese Surplus Population.'
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference Sheet Regarding Report on Japanese Surplus Population Problem

subfiles.about: Military intelligence report on Japan's 1937 population statistics, sex ratios, imperial growth, and principal cities.
subfiles.from: John Beckerling and William C. Crane
subfiles.summary: War Department G-2 report evaluates 1937 figures: Japan proper's population at 71,252,500 (up about one million), with the Empire and sphere of control estimated at 101,500,000, plus figures for the six largest cities.
subfiles.title: War Department G-2 Report No. 9096 on 1937 Population Statistics

subfiles.about: Consular survey of population, household counts, sex distribution, and municipal expansion in Aichi Prefecture and the City of Nagoya.
subfiles.summary: Vice Consul Stephan reports 1937 registration data for Aichi Prefecture: females outnumber males by 7% overall (except Nagoya), and reviews Nagoya's growth to 1,219,550 residents as the Empire's third largest city ahead of its 1939 anniversary.
subfiles.title: Consular Report by Stephan on Population of Aichi Prefecture and Nagoya
